priorityRule: Two co-equal pillars, Tea and Masala, interleaved rather than cascaded (CLAUDE.md §7.2, amended): Blue Tea (1) > Spices (2) > Red Tea (3) > Combo Packs (4) > Black Tea (5). products.description:
Black pepper, often called the “King of Spices,” is one of the most widely used spices in the world. Known for its sharp, pungent flavor and aroma, it adds heat and depth to both savory and sweet dishes.

Key Characteristics:

Flavor: Sharp, hot, and mildly woody with a lingering heat.
Aroma: Strong, warm, and slightly earthy.
Texture: Whole peppercorns or finely ground powder.
Color: Black to dark brown.

Culinary Uses:

Seasoning: A staple spice for enhancing the flavor of almost any dish.
Soups & Stews: Adds warmth and depth to broths and gravies.
Marinades & Rubs: Commonly used in meat, poultry, and seafood preparations.
Pickles: Used in traditional pickling recipes for added spice.
Baked Goods & Snacks: Adds a subtle kick to biscuits, crackers, and spiced snacks.

Health Benefits:

Rich in Piperine: Enhances nutrient absorption and supports digestion.
Antioxidant Properties: Protects the body from free radical damage.
Anti-inflammatory Effects: May help reduce inflammation and support joint health.
Boosts Metabolism: Linked to improved metabolism and weight management.

Storage:

Store whole peppercorns in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.
Whole peppercorns retain flavor longer than ground pepper.
For best taste, grind peppercorns fresh before use.

products.description:
Garam masala is a traditional Indian spice blend made from a mix of aromatic spices. Known for its warm, rich, and complex flavor, it enhances the taste of curries, stews, and a wide variety of dishes.

Key Characteristics:

Flavor: Warm, aromatic, and slightly sweet with hints of spice.
Aroma: Strong, earthy, and fragrant.
Texture: Finely ground powder, though some variations use coarse blends.
Color: Brown to dark brown depending on the spices used.

Culinary Uses:

Curries & Gravies: Enhances depth and aroma in Indian curries.
Soups & Stews: Adds warmth and complexity to broths and stews.
Rice Dishes: Commonly sprinkled over biryanis and pulao.
Snacks & Street Food: Brings bold flavor to chaats and fried snacks.
Marinades: Mixed with yogurt or oil to prepare spiced marinades for meats and vegetables.

Health Benefits:

Digestive Aid: Ingredients like cumin and cardamom support digestion.
Rich in Antioxidants: Helps fight free radicals and boost immunity.
Anti-inflammatory Properties: Spices like cloves and cinnamon may help reduce inflammation.
Metabolism Booster: Black pepper and cinnamon may support metabolism and weight management.

Storage:

Store garam masala in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.
To retain its aroma and freshness, avoid direct sunlight and moisture.
Best used within 3–6 months for maximum flavor.

products.description:
Turmeric is a vibrant yellow spice derived from the root of the Curcuma longa plant. It has been used for centuries in Ayurvedic medicine and cooking, prized for its medicinal properties and distinct flavor.

Key Characteristics:

Flavor: Earthy, slightly bitter, and with a hint of pepper.
Aroma: Warm and slightly pungent.
Appearance: Bright yellow powder or root.
Texture: Smooth and slightly oily.

Culinary Uses:

Curries: Turmeric is a key ingredient in many Indian and Asian curries, imparting its signature color and flavor.
Marinades: It adds a unique flavor to marinades for meats and vegetables.
Pickles: Turmeric is often used to preserve and color pickles.
Baking: It can be used in baking to add a subtle flavor and a golden hue to baked goods.
Drinks: Turmeric is a popular ingredient in golden milk, a soothing and flavorful drink.

Health Benefits:

Anti-inflammatory properties: Turmeric contains curcumin, a compound with powerful anti-inflammatory properties.
Antioxidant: It is rich in antioxidants that help protect cells from damage.
Digestive aid: Turmeric can help improve digestion and reduce bloating.
Liver health: Some studies suggest it may support liver health.
Brain health: It may have potential benefits for brain health and cognitive function.

products.description:
Red chili peppers are a popular spice known for their intense heat and vibrant color. They are a staple in many cuisines around the world, adding a fiery kick to dishes.

Key Characteristics:

Flavor: Spicy, pungent, and slightly bitter.
Heat: Varies depending on the specific variety, from mild to extremely hot.
Appearance: Slender and elongated, often with a curved shape.
Color: Red, but can range from green to orange depending on ripeness.

Culinary Uses:

Sauces and pastes: Red chili peppers are a primary ingredient in hot sauces, chili paste, and salsa.
Curries and stews: They add heat and flavor to curries, stews, and soups.
Marinades and rubs: Used to marinate meats and create flavorful rubs.
Pickles: They add a spicy kick to pickled vegetables.
Toppings: Often used as a topping for tacos, pizza, and other dishes.

Health Benefits:

Capsaicin: The compound responsible for heat in chili peppers has been linked to various health benefits, including pain relief and improved metabolism.
Antioxidants: Red chili peppers contain antioxidants that help protect cells from damage.

Storage:

Store red chili peppers in a cool, dry place in an airtight container.
To preserve their heat and flavor, they can be dried or frozen.

products.description:
Coriander is a popular herb and spice used in countless cuisines worldwide. It offers a unique blend of sweet, citrusy, and slightly peppery flavors that enhance dishes in various ways.

Key Characteristics:

Leaves: Commonly known as cilantro, they have a fresh, herbaceous aroma and a bright, citrusy taste.
Seeds: Also called coriander seeds, they are dried fruits with a warm, nutty, and slightly spicy flavor.
Appearance: Leaves are green and feathery, while seeds are small, round, and brownish-yellow.

Culinary Uses:

Fresh Leaves (Cilantro):
Used as a garnish for various dishes.
Added to salsas, guacamole, and chimichurri sauce.
Incorporated into Mexican, Indian, and Thai cuisine.
Dried Seeds:
Ground into a powder for use in spice blends like garam masala.
Added to curries, stews, and marinades.
Used in pickling and preserving.
Often paired with cumin, turmeric, and chili powder.

Health Benefits:

Antioxidant Properties: Coriander is rich in antioxidants that help protect cells from damage.
Digestive Aid: It can aid digestion and relieve symptoms like bloating and gas.
Anti-inflammatory Effects: Some studies suggest coriander may have anti-inflammatory properties.

Storage:

Fresh Leaves: Store in a refrigerator in a sealed container for up to a week.
Dried Seeds: Keep in a cool, dry place in an airtight container.
